items.action: Patch internet-facing PHP to a fixed release now and hunt for signs of compromise; treat Apache mod_php deployments as highest risk.
items.details: The flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution and are reported at CVSS 9.2. Fixed releases are PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; exploitation leading to remote code execution was detected against an Apache mod_php installation in a honeypot on October 25.
items.summary: CISA added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue after confirming live exploitation, with a patch deadline of Thursday, October 29 for US federal civilian agencies.
items.title: CISA adds PHP2Shell flaws to KEV; patch by Oct 29

items.action: Update NeMo Agent Toolkit to 1.9.0 and TensorRT-LLM to 1.3.0rc25, and restrict any unpatched toolkit instances from untrusted networks.
items.details: According to NVIDIA, the flaw could lead to code execution, privilege escalation, data tampering, denial of service and information disclosure. The update fixes six flaws in total across NeMo Agent Toolkit, TensorRT-LLM and PhysX; no active exploitation was confirmed in the reporting.
items.summary: NVIDIA's October 27 security update patches CVE-2026-65145, a missing-authentication flaw in NeMo Agent Toolkit scored CVSS 10.0 that lets a remote attacker act with no login.
items.title: NVIDIA patches CVSS 10.0 flaw in NeMo Agent Toolkit

items.action: Upgrade MLflow to 3.17.0 and never expose an unauthenticated MLflow server to untrusted networks.
items.details: The flaw affects MLflow 3.12.0rc0 through versions before 3.17.0. On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow image, exploitation produced arbitrary Python code execution as the server process, which runs as root in the reproduced image. The same October 27 disclosure included an arbitrary file-read flaw (CVE-2026-116690, CVSS 7.5) and an API-key logging flaw (CVE-2026-116691).
items.summary: CVE-2026-116692, disclosed October 27, lets an unauthenticated attacker achieve remote code execution on MLflow servers through third-party scorer deserialization; it is patched in MLflow 3.17.0.
items.title: Critical MLflow RCE gives root on unauthenticated servers

items.action: Check device firmware for GoAhead 6.1.1 or later and press vendors for updated firmware, especially for equipment using mutual TLS.
items.details: The most severe is CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS 9.1): GoAhead loads a certificate revocation list but never enables revocation checking on OpenSSL-compatible builds. The other two score 7.4 and 5.9. All are fixed in GoAhead 6.1.1, released to device makers on August 2 with advisories published October 12; GoAhead runs in hundreds of millions of devices from vendors including Palo Alto Networks, Siemens, Honeywell and Boeing.
items.summary: Three TLS integration flaws in the GoAhead embedded web server, disclosed by FoxIO on October 26, can leave revoked client certificates accepted, encrypted sessions recoverable, or a chain-depth limit unenforced, depending on the TLS backend built into the device.
items.title: GoAhead TLS flaws put hundreds of millions of devices at risk

items.action: Customers should follow GMO's guidance on scanning, backing up and disconnecting affected devices, and should not share any disclosed information.
items.details: The access targeted the Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service, with up to 26,739 servers potentially affected. GMO said the attackers claim they will keep releasing information daily at noon; it will offer a special consolation payment of up to 3 million yen to customers whose personal information is exposed and a reward of up to $1 million for information identifying the perpetrators.
items.summary: GMO Internet said on October 27 that personal information believed to belong to a customer was disclosed by those behind unauthorised access to its systems, after the company did not meet a noon deadline tied to a $50 million cryptocurrency demand it refuses to pay.
items.title: GMO customer data disclosed after $50 million demand refused

items.action: Affected customers should change reused passwords and watch for phishing using the exposed personal details.
items.details: The exposed records include names, telephone numbers, email addresses, user IDs, dates of birth, gender and internet connection IDs, and 16 sets of bank account details. The company said passwords for the general membership records were not leaked and no credit-card data was involved; the access occurred on October 19 and PlayStation Network accounts were not affected.
items.summary: Sony Network Communications disclosed on October 27 that unauthorised access to its So-net member database exposed 2,585,481 member records across So-net and plala S Course, plus email addresses and passwords for 54,401 email accounts.
items.title: Sony Network Communications discloses breach of 2.58 million records

items.action: Treat the listing as an unverified claim; affected organisations should verify independently before acting on the alleged data categories.
items.details: The claim, as reported from the leak-site listing, describes social-welfare and migration client files, nursing-home medical files, civil-status records, payslips and database backups. The claim remains unverified and no independent confirmation from the municipality was cited in the reporting.
items.summary: Rhysida listed the Belgian municipality of Machelen on its leak site on October 27, claiming about 1.3 million files totalling roughly 2.9 TB from municipal and social-welfare (OCMW) file servers.
items.title: Rhysida lists Belgian municipality of Machelen (claim)

items.action: Hospitals should isolate affected systems, preserve logs for investigators, and verify backups before any restore.
items.details: A notepad message on screen identified the group as 'Crypto 24' and claimed sensitive data had been stolen and encrypted, with a 3-to-7-day ultimatum and a threat to leak data on a Tor site. Police said the complaint does not disclose the amount of ransom allegedly demanded.
items.summary: A cyberattack in the early hours of October 18 encrypted all nine servers at Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, disrupting its hospital management system, billing, insurance claims and government-scheme benefits; the incident was reported on October 27.
items.title: Ransomware attack encrypts 9 servers at Kamalnayan Bajaj Hospital

items.action: Apply the out-of-band update (KB5134133 for Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H2, KB5134125 for Windows 10 21H2/22H2) on systems without automatic trust updates and check dependent certificates.
items.details: The same seven certificates were scheduled for removal from the Edge trust list on October 27. The updates are aimed particularly at systems that cannot receive automatic certificate trust updates, such as disconnected environments; organisations using certificates chaining to the removed roots should inventory them and arrange replacements.
items.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band Windows updates on October 26 removing seven certificates — six eMudhra G3 roots and an AAA Certificate Services cross-sign — from the Windows trust list, following the exposure of eight weak eMudhra intermediate CA private keys.
items.title: Microsoft's out-of-band update removes trust in 7 eMudhra certificates

items.action: Update Chrome to the latest available version on all desktops and prioritise systems where browsing is used for sensitive work.
items.details: The advisory lists use-after-free errors, memory corruption, improper input validation, out-of-bounds read and write, type confusion, range errors and information leaks. An attacker could exploit the flaws by getting a user to open a specially crafted web request.
items.summary: CERT-In's advisory CIVN-2026-0524, published October 26, rates several Chrome vulnerabilities on Windows, macOS and Linux as critical and warns they could allow arbitrary code execution, information disclosure, security bypass or denial of service.
items.title: CERT-In flags critical Chrome flaws; update now
